title: Repeated halving after a countdown
statement: Let $A$ be a register program, let $l,l_x,l_1,l_2$ be labels, and let $c,r$ be distinct registers. Suppose label $l$ tests whether register $c$ is zero, its positive branch decrements $c$ and goes to $l_2$, and $l_2$ halves register $r$ and returns to $l$. For every $k\in\mathbb N$ and register assignment $v$ with $v(c)=k$ and $v(s)\le B$ for every register $s$, the program can reach the configuration at $l_x$ obtained by setting $c$ to zero and replacing $r$ by $v(r)/2^{v(c)}$, with no result bit, while every configuration before the final one satisfies the guard requiring the program's precondition and all registers to be at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: The transition at $l$ is a zero test on $c$ with branches $l_x$ and $l_1$
The transition at $l_1$ decrements $c$ and goes to $l_2$
The transition at $l_2$ halves $r$ and returns to $l$
Every register value in $v$ is at most $B$
